description: PRD-218 — Framework Upgrade & CSP Nonce Hardening (the deferred infra slice split out of PRD-200). Two findings: (1) Next.js 14.2.35 carries HIGH DoS (Server Components / HTTP request deserialization) + HIGH SSRF-in-server-actions advisories — cleared at 15.5.x (AC-1). NOTE 14.2.35 is ALREADY the latest 14.2.x, so the PRD's 14.2.x-patch fallback does NOT exist — clearing the HIGH advisories REQUIRES the 15.x major bump (Node floor >=18.18; repo .nvmrc=20, Node 20.20 available via nvm). (2) CSP retains script-src 'unsafe-inline' (MEDIUM) — migrate to a per-request nonce so a missed XSS sink still cannot execute (AC-2). CSP today is STATIC in next.config.js headers() (base/admin/store variants); a per-request nonce MUST move to middleware.ts (config headers cannot vary per request). 'unsafe-inline' exists because Clerk + Next inject inline scripts, so the nonce must propagate to <ClerkProvider nonce> + every <Script>. App lives in nextjs_space/ (pnpm 10, Next 14.2.35, React 18.2, Clerk, Prisma 6.7). NO Vitest on main — US-001 stands up a minimal unit harness. Source PRD: docs/PRDS/REMEDIATION/PRD-218-framework-upgrade-csp-nonce-hardening.md. BROWSER-SMOKE + MAJOR-DECISION GATES (PRD OQ-1/OQ-2/AC-1a/AC-2b) are owned by Gerard and recorded as human follow-ups in progress.txt — do NOT falsely mark a browser-verified AC done; this in-session build delivers the safe, unit/build-verifiable slice and prepares the bump on the worktree. Global rules: immutable updates; client errors via apiError()/apiValidationError() (no raw error leak); no console.log in prod code (console.error ok); no @ts-ignore/as any; keep style-src 'unsafe-inline' (only script-src must drop it per AC-2); NEVER git add -A, commit .env*, or touch main/other worktrees; do NOT run the autonomous --dangerously-skip-permissions loop.

acceptanceCriteria: In middleware.ts generate nonce = generateNonce() once per request; set requestHeaders.set('x-nonce', nonce); choose variant by path (store=/store/*, admin=/tenant-admin/analytics + /super-admin/analytics, else base)
Attach Content-Security-Policy (buildCsp) to the response on EVERY return path (NextResponse.next / NextResponse.rewrite / json) via a small helper so no path is missed

Remove the Content-Security-Policy entries from next.config.js headers() (KEEP the other security headers: X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, COOP/CORP, X-Frame-Options); avoid emitting two CSP headers
